title: Momentum and its conservation
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics 1 (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: D09-ap1#t2 term and clue written for the game; D09-ap1#t4 term and clue written for the game; D09-ap1#t3 term and clue written for the game; D09-ap1#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: D09-ap1#N.2, D09-ap1#N.6, D09-ap1#N.8, D09-ap1#N.10.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Environment
items.clue: Where momentum flows to or from when the net external force is not zero.

items.label: Impulse
items.clue: Change in momentum that a third-law pair delivers equally and oppositely to A and B.

items.label: Inelastic collision
items.clue: Impact in which nonconservative internal forces turn K into thermal energy and sound.

items.label: Collision model
items.clue: Approximation that ignores external forces during a brief impact, as internal ones are far larger.

questions.stem: Two carts move along a straight track. Cart 1, of mass 3.0 kg, moves at +2.0 m/s, and cart 2, of mass 2.0 kg, moves at −1.0 m/s. What is the total momentum of the two-cart system?

A cart of mass m moves with speed v along a level track toward a wall. It hits the wall and rebounds along the same line with speed v/3. Taking the cart's initial direction of motion as positive and the cart as the system, which expression gives the momentum transferred to the system from its surroundings during the collision?

Cart 1 rolls along a level track toward an identical cart 2, which is at rest. After they collide, cart 1 is at rest and cart 2 moves off with cart 1's original velocity. A student says that the collision cannot be elastic, because cart 1's kinetic energy changed. Which response to the student is correct?

options.text: Only the total kinetic energy of the two carts must be unchanged, and it is.
The student is right: in an elastic collision each cart keeps its kinetic energy.
Every collision conserves kinetic energy, since total energy is conserved.
The total momentum is unchanged, and that shows kinetic energy is too.

questions.stem: A box slides across a level floor and comes to rest because of friction. Which statement about the box's momentum is correct?

options.text: It was transferred to the Earth by friction, so the box–Earth total did not change.
It was destroyed by friction, which turned it into thermal energy in the box and floor.
It was not conserved, since momentum is conserved only in collisions and explosions.
It was transferred to the Earth, which gained the speed that the box lost.
